So before the hard conversation, write down the one thing you need them to walk away with. Say that. Let the rest go.

{"text": ""You need to be more strategic."

If you have ever walked out of a review with that sentence and no idea what to do with it, you are not alone. Most leaders cannot give feedback with an example attached. And most employees do not know they are allowed to ask for one.

So ask. Calmly. Can you give me an example?

If they have one, you now have something real to work on. If it is crickets, you have learned the feedback was a feeling, and feelings can be reshaped. Either way, you walked out with evidence instead of a verdict.

This is the kind of inside work we are doing on Thursday, October 29 at 7 PM ET in The Corporate Advantage, a free live masterclass. Link in bio.

{"text": "Here is a leadership habit I learned early and have never regretted.

Before you correct someone, go look. Not at what a peer told you. Not at what you assume. At the work itself. You inspect what you expect, and then you have the conversation from facts.

It takes ten more minutes. It saves you a good employee, and it saves you from being the leader who manages by rumor.

{"text": "Every productivity system I have ever used, I learned in a minivan.

Pick them up, get them changed, get myself changed, get everybody where they need to be, and still walk in on time. Nothing in corporate America has asked more of my calendar than that.

So when someone tells me they cannot find the time, I ask a different question: what are you treating as optional that a mother would not?

Moms in leadership, I see you. {"text": "Sunday thought.

I believe He is in control. That gives me peace most people are looking for in all the wrong places. But I have watched too many people turn that peace into a parking spot. I prayed about it. The Lord will handle it. And then nothing moves.

Faith is an active word. He does His part. He expects you to show up for yours.

{"text": "Doing your job well is not good enough. I know how that sounds. Follow me for a second.

Every role we post draws thousands of applicants. The screening stops the moment the pile has five solid candidates, and the inside referral almost always makes that pile. Not because the resume was better. Because somebody in the building could vouch for them.

That is not unfair. It is how trust works. And it means your network is the part of your career most people never manage on purpose.

If your network lives only inside your company, you have one investment. Diversify. One conversation a week with someone who does not sign your paycheck.

We go deeper on this Thursday, October 29 at 7 PM ET in The Corporate Advantage, free and live. Link in bio.
